_what: Where troid hides its affiliate links (launch handoff 5.3; the owner's decision, 2026-10-03). A link is hidden in a country on any of the three lists below; the calculator, the compare and every figure are the same in every country. /api/where gives the visitor's country (Vercel's x-vercel-ip-country); every affiliate link waits for it and stays hidden when it can't be read (fail closed). A VPN defeats this: it is a good-faith measure, not a guarantee (/faq#regions). Read by backtest/geo.py, which builds the pages' check, and by the /sources page; web/test_geo.py holds it.
decided_by: the owner, on troid's recommendation (launch handoff 5.3)

firm_terms.title: The firm's own terms
firm_terms.basis: The countries each firm's own terms exclude, as troid recorded them in firms.json (availability.excluded), with the document and the date troid read it there. A country troid didn't read in the firm's terms (availability.not_from_terms) never hides a link, and neither does an exclusion for one trading platform (availability.platform: MT5 for US residents), which the calculator states instead.
firm_terms.caveat: Bitfunded's Terms list no excluded countries (4(b) puts local law on the trader); a third-party review lists some, which troid hasn't read in Bitfunded's own documents, so they hide nothing.

embargo.title: Comprehensive embargoes
embargo.basis: Jurisdictions under comprehensive US sanctions programmes. troid sends no one there to buy from any firm, whatever the firm's terms say.

source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
source.title: Sanctions Programs and Country Information

embargo.caveat: A country-level list: a sanctioned region inside a country (Crimea, for one) can't be told apart by the visitor's country, and isn't listed.

law.title: Local law on promoting these products
law.basis: Countries where troid's launch research found that promoting prop challenges or paying offshore trading venues is restricted. troid recommended hiding the links there until counsel says otherwise; the owner decided it on 2026-10-03.

CN.why: mainland China's ban on crypto trading services, reaffirmed in November 2025

BD.why: Bangladesh's foreign-exchange law bars residents from paying offshore crypto and forex venues

FR.why: article 4 of the 9 June 2023 influencer law bans promoting financial contracts and digital-asset services without AMF registration or authorisation

AE.why: SCA Resolution 10 of 2025 requires a licence to publish financial content to UAE audiences

IN.why: the RBI's alert list of unauthorised forex platforms; FEMA penalties fall on residents who trade on them

ID.why: Bappebti's licensing regime, under which unlicensed forex domains are routinely blocked

EG.why: Egypt's licence requirement for financial promotion (Law 194 of 2020)

law.caveat: troid's research (September 2026) summarised these; not every primary text was read (the UAE article and Egypt's Law 194/2020 were not), and counsel hasn't reviewed the list. A country without a link here has the research's summary only.
